summary: Evergrande Auto's delisting from the stock market sent shockwaves through the industry, as the Guangzhou Auto Show entered a密集新车发布期: BMW launched its Neue Klasse dual models, Great Wall's WEY brand unveiled multiple new cars, and the range race broke through the 1,000-kilometer barrier.

articles.title: Evergrande Auto Stripped of Listing Status, Automotive Dream Ends in Delisting
articles.summary: Evergrande Auto has been officially delisted, ending the listing run of a once multi-billion-yuan new energy vehicle player.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, Evergrande Auto's listing status has been revoked, marking the formal departure of the highly anticipated cross-industry carmaker from the capital markets. Backed by the financial muscle of China Evergrande Group, the company had invested heavily in new energy vehicle manufacturing, once planning a full product lineup covering sedans and SUVs and building production bases in Tianjin and other locations. However, weighed down by its parent's debt crisis, Evergrande Auto long struggled with funding shortages, difficulties in mass production and delivery, and sustained operating losses, while efforts to resume trading and restructure debt repeatedly stalled. The delisting now draws a definitive line under its capital markets journey. Its trajectory from high-profile entry to abrupt exit has become the most cautionary case of the recent wave of cross-industry carmaking.
articles.impact: Evergrande Auto's delisting sounds a warning for the cross-industry carmaking boom. Capital and industrial resources will increasingly concentrate among leading automakers with real mass-production capability and self-sustaining cash flow, accelerating an industry shakeout.

articles.title: WEY Debuts Three Cars at Guangzhou Auto Show, V9X EV Opens Pre-Orders, Second-Gen Lanshan Launching Soon
articles.summary: WEY unveiled three new cars in one go at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with pre-orders for the V9X EV opening simultaneously and the second-generation Lanshan set to launch soon.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, WEY launched a full-scale product offensive at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with three new cars debuting on the same stage. The V9X EV officially opened for pre-orders; as the pure-electric version of WEY's MPV lineup, it further completes the brand's new-energy product matrix. The highly anticipated second-generation Lanshan is also about to launch. As WEY's flagship model in the mid-to-large new-energy SUV segment, the redesigned vehicle is expected to receive comprehensive upgrades in intelligent features and its battery, motor and electronic control systems. The simultaneous rollout of three cars demonstrates Great Wall Motor's premium brand's determination to fully transition toward electrification and intelligence, and reflects WEY's strategy of using product density to grab market share in the fiercely competitive new-energy market.
articles.impact: WEY's intensive rollout of new models across both pure-electric and hybrid lines will put it in direct competition with rivals such as Li Auto and AITO in the RMB300,000-class new-energy SUV and MPV segments, giving consumers more choices.

articles.title: Great Wall's HEV Family Debuts Collectively at Guangzhou Auto Show, Multiple New Cars Unveiled
articles.summary: Great Wall Motor's HEV family made a collective appearance at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with multiple new hybrid-electric models debuting and drawing attention.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Great Wall Motor's HEV family appeared together at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with multiple new cars launching at once. Beyond its pure-electric strategy, Great Wall showcased its HEV hybrid product lineup with high profile, reflecting its continued commitment to hybrid technology. HEV models require no external charging and deliver strong fuel economy, giving them a unique advantage in lower-tier markets and export markets where charging infrastructure remains underdeveloped. Great Wall's family-style presentation of HEV products shows its intent to cover a broader consumer base with a hybrid matrix spanning multiple models and price points, hedging the market risk of a single pure-electric path through technological diversification during the new-energy transition period.
articles.impact: Great Wall's push into the HEV route underscores that the hybrid market remains a key growth engine, particularly favorable for export and lower-tier markets, and is expected to serve as a stabilizer in Great Wall's sales structure.

articles.title: Show Floor Photos: BYD Whale EV Offers Over 900km Range
articles.summary: First photos of BYD's Whale at the auto show reveal an EV version with a range exceeding 900 kilometers.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto's auto show photo coverage, BYD's new model, the Whale, appeared on the stand, with its EV version offering a range of over 900km — leading among pure-electric models in its class. As a new model under BYD's Ocean lineup, the Whale draws on the company's long-standing expertise in core EV technologies such as Blade Battery and e-Platform 3.0, showing strong competitiveness in range, energy consumption and cabin space. The 900km-plus figure also indicates that BYD is continuing to optimize battery energy density and overall vehicle energy management, further easing range anxiety for EV users. The Whale's launch is expected to enrich BYD's product offerings in the mainstream pure-electric segment and exert direct pressure on rivals.
articles.impact: A 900km-plus range raises the bar for mainstream pure-electric models once again, accelerating the phase-out of low-range vehicles and creating clear technological pressure on competitors at the same price points.

articles.title: 2027 Cadillac XT5 Launched With Limited-Time Price From RMB215,900
articles.summary: The 2027 Cadillac XT5 has officially launched, with limited-time promotional pricing starting at RMB215,900.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the 2027 Cadillac XT5 has officially launched, with a limited-time starting price of RMB215,900. As SAIC-GM Cadillac's volume model in the mid-size luxury SUV market, the new XT5 enters the market at under RMB220,000 — a price that has slipped into mainstream joint-venture brand SUV territory, revealing a clear tendency among luxury brands to trade price for volume amid intense competition. Against the continued squeeze from premium new-energy SUVs from domestic brands, traditional luxury brands' gasoline and hybrid models are maintaining market share through annual refreshes bundled with purchase incentives, while terminal pricing systems face ongoing restructuring.
articles.impact: Luxury SUV prices falling into the RMB210,000 range will further squeeze the room for joint-venture and domestic premium gasoline SUVs, continuing to improve value for money for car buyers.

articles.title: BMW's Neue Klasse Era Kicks Off in Full: Nearly 20 New Cars to Launch in China Within a Year
articles.summary: BMW has announced an accelerated Neue Klasse strategy, with nearly 20 new models set to roll out into the Chinese market over the next year.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, BMW's Neue Klasse strategy is fully underway, with nearly 20 new models due to launch in China within the next year. Centered on the Neue Klasse platform, BMW is comprehensively overhauling the technical foundation of its electrification, digitalization and driving experience, while rolling out an unprecedented density of product launches in China. The nearly 20 new models span battery-electric, gasoline and plug-in hybrid powertrains, underscoring BMW's strong emphasis on China, the world's largest single market. Against the backdrop of rapidly rising domestic new-energy brands and a reshaping competitive landscape in the luxury segment, BMW has chosen a high-density product offensive to defend its position in China, while accelerating localized R&D and supply chain build-out.
articles.impact: BMW is countering the surge from domestic brands with nearly 20 new launches, kicking off a new round of product warfare in the luxury market as competition on pricing and features intensifies.

articles.title: New-Generation BMW iX3 and i3 Launched: From 269,900 and 249,900 Yuan, Up to 1,028 km Range
articles.summary: The new-generation BMW iX3 starts at 269,900 yuan and the i3 at 249,900 yuan, with the i3 offering up to 1,028 km of range.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the new-generation BMW iX3 has officially launched at a starting price of 269,900 yuan, equipped with the Momenta R7 intelligent driving solution; the new-generation BMW i3 launched alongside it at a starting price of 249,900 yuan, with a maximum range of up to 1,028 km. The two models are key milestones for the BMW Neue Klasse platform in China. The i3's breakthrough of the 1,000 km range is particularly striking, placing it directly in the top tier of battery-electric sedans, while the iX3 addresses BMW's product gap in advanced smart driving through the Momenta R7 solution, reflecting a new model of deep collaboration between international luxury brands and Chinese tech companies.
articles.impact: With pricing from 249,900 yuan and 1,000 km-range capability, BMW is charging directly into the heartland of domestic brands while strengthening its smart-driving capabilities via Momenta, significantly raising the intensity of competition in the premium EV market.

articles.title: Hyundai IONIQ Mercury Concept Debuts at Guangzhou Auto Show; Production Version Due Next Year
articles.summary: Hyundai's IONIQ Mercury concept made its China debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with the production version planned for launch next year.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Hyundai's IONIQ brand unveiled its all-new concept car, the IONIQ Mercury, at the Guangzhou Auto Show, with the production version scheduled to launch next year. The IONIQ Mercury concept showcases Hyundai's latest thinking on pure-electric design language, smart cockpit and battery/motor/electronics technology, serving as an important product milestone in its electrification strategy. Amid intense competition in China's new-energy vehicle market, Hyundai is seeking breakthroughs by speeding up new product introductions and strengthening the independent image of the IONIQ brand, aiming to regain relevance in China through differentiated design and a global technology platform.
articles.impact: Hyundai is accelerating its EV product cadence; if the production version delivers competitive pricing and capability, it could establish a new competitive foothold in the joint-venture EV market.

articles.title: Tesla Launches New Vehicle Financing Plans; Xiaomi Delivers 100,000 New Cars in Q3
articles.summary: Tesla rolls out new financing schemes to boost orders, while Xiaomi hits 100,000 new-car deliveries in the third quarter.
articles.detail: According to Auto Morning Post, Tesla has launched new vehicle financing plans, adjusting financial policies to lower the barrier to purchase and drive conversion of end-market orders. As competition in the NEV market intensifies and the price war gradually shifts into a battle of financing and service, financing schemes are becoming a key tool for automakers to lift sales. Meanwhile, Xiaomi Auto delivered 100,000 new vehicles in the third quarter, showing that both its capacity ramp-up and market acceptance have exceeded industry expectations, firmly placing it in the top tier of new-force deliverers. One leading brand is using financial tools to stabilize orders, the other is using delivery volume to prove scale effects — reflecting a broader shift in the NEV market from pure price competition toward overall strength competition.
articles.impact: Financing schemes have become a new competitive lever, and delivery scale determines cost competitiveness. The Matthew effect in the NEV market is intensifying, putting further pressure on second-tier brands.

articles.title: Interview with Jiang Ping: No High- and Low-Trim Safety Split — Changan Aims to Make Safety Tech Universally Accessible
articles.summary: Changan Auto's Jiang Ping said in an interview that safety configurations should not be tiered by trim level, and that safety technology should be made universally accessible.
articles.detail: In an interview with NetEase Auto, Changan Auto's Jiang Ping stated that the company's product safety philosophy explicitly rejects splitting safety features between high and low trims — meaning core technologies in both active and passive safety should not vary by vehicle price point, and safety technology should be universally available. This statement addresses a common practice in the auto industry, where advanced safety and intelligent driving features are often concentrated in higher trims. Changan's strategy is to treat safety capability as a fundamental brand competitiveness, using scale and platform-based approaches to spread costs and bring safety technologies previously reserved for premium models down to mainstream-priced products. With consumer safety awareness rising and safety incidents having an outsized impact on brands, safety is emerging as a new anchor of product value.
articles.impact: If the concept of universal safety access is implemented, it could force the entire industry to raise safety standards for entry-level models, with safety configurations becoming a core selling point in the next phase of product competition.

articles.title: Range Race Enters the 1,000-Kilometer Era as BEV Elimination Heats Up
articles.summary: BMW i3 hits 1,028 km and BYD Sea Whale exceeds 900 km, pushing the EV range race into a new phase.
articles.detail: According to the dense stream of new vehicle launches at the Guangzhou Auto Show today, the range race for battery-electric vehicles has officially entered the 1,000-kilometer era: the new-generation BMW i3 offers up to 1,028 km of range, while the BYD Sea Whale EV exceeds 900 km. As mainstream automakers continue to breakthrough in battery energy density, vehicle-level energy consumption management and thermal management systems, long range is gradually trickling down from premium models to mainstream price segments. It can be predicted that within the next year, BEV models with less than 600 km of range will rapidly lose competitiveness in the retail market, while 1,000-kilometer-class models are expected to gain ground quickly in the 200,000 to 300,000 yuan segment, driving the pure-electric market into a new round of product elimination.
articles.impact: A fast-rising range threshold will accelerate the clearing out of low-range models, while placing higher demands on supporting industries such as charging networks and battery recycling.

articles.title: HEV and BEV Advance in Parallel as Diversified Tech Paths Become Automakers' Winter Consensus
articles.summary: Great Wall doubles down on HEV while BYD and BMW focus on BEV, making diversified technology routes a common choice amid uncertainty.
articles.detail: Observations from multiple launches at today's Guangzhou Auto Show show a clear trend of diversification in mainstream automakers' technology route choices: Great Wall Motor is boosting its hybrid lineup with a collective debut of its HEV family, while the WEY brand continues to advance electrification and intelligence with models such as the V9X EV. BYD and BMW are respectively strengthening their BEV offensive with the Sea Whale and the new-generation i3/iX3. This indicates that under multiple factors — including subsidy cuts, uneven regional charging infrastructure and regulatory differences in export markets — no single technology route can cover the entire market demand. Over the coming year, automakers with full technology reserves spanning BEV, plug-in hybrid, extended-range and HEV will enjoy stronger risk resilience and market adaptability.
articles.impact: Full technology-route capability will become a core competitiveness for automakers, while brands with a narrow technology portfolio will see their room for survival steadily squeezed amid market volatility.
